newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end up, erase loss from scandal worry.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end up, erase loss from scandal worry.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended higher on Thursday as buying of blue chips accelerated in late afternoon, erasing losses created by racketeer scandal worries and a limping construction sector, brokers said.
The Nikkei 225 ended 118.61 points or 0.59 percent higher at 20,331.43. Its September futures jumped 110 to 20,330.

"Some bellwether issues kept rising as some market participants bought on end-month window dressing," said Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager. "Sentiment is looking a bit better, but there were few new reasons to keep buying."
Brokers said more powerful factors were needed to boost the market as a whole, such as signs of strength in the economy or a revision in land policies.
"The downside of the market should be fairly limited as U.S. stocks are still rising and Japanese blue chips are bargains in comparison," Dai-Ichi's Orimi said.

The TOPIX index rose 7.12 points or 0.46 percent to end at 1,544.04. The Nikkei 300 added 1.89 points or 0.63 percent to reach 301.93. The second section index shed 1.04 points or 0.06 percent to 1,769.29. Turnover was 9.34 million shares, compared with 7.53 million in the previous session.
The over-the-counter index was down 4.50 points or 0.40 percent at 1,125.35 in late Tokyo.
